subject: Response tiers & contract options for Dedicated deployment
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah@brighthealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brighthealth.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Premium support / uptime tiers for Dedicated (BrightHealth)

Hi Ava / Diego,

Thanks for the demo last week. Were moving quickly on our evaluation and need a clear pricing + terms answer for premium support options for a Dedicated deployment. Specific asks:
- Uptime tiers you offer (monthly target and how measured) and the service credit formula if you miss targets.
- Response / remediation SLAs for P1/P2 incidents (including time-to-first-response and time-to-recovery expectations).
- Escalation coverage: is 24/7 on-call included for the top tier? Are named escalation contacts provided?
- Any exclusions (scheduled maintenance windows, agreed maintenance, force majeure) and whether credits are retroactive.
- Pricing for each tier and whether an enterprise discount applies for a 12- or 24-month reserved commit.

Were working toward an internal procurement deadline of May 20 and comparing Redwood against two other vendors. I attached our support questionnaire (BrightHealth_Support_Request_May2026.pdf). Can you send a written summary and a sample SOW with pricing by EOD May 13?

Thanks,

Sarah Lin
Head of Cloud Ops, BrightHealth

Attachments: BrightHealth_Support_Request_May2026.pdf

From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@brighthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Premium support / uptime tiers for Dedicated (BrightHealth)

Hi Sarah,

Appreciate the clear list — we'll get you a concise written summary and a sample SOW. High-level answers to start:
- We offer three primary tiers for Dedicated: Standard, Premium, and Platinum. Measurement is based on regional availability telemetry (per-region uptime) with a 30-day rolling window.
- Service credits scale by missed availability (we'll provide the exact percentages in the doc).
- Response SLAs: P1 = 15 min to acknowledge, P2 = 1 hour to acknowledge (detailed remediation targets vary by tier).
- Platinum includes 24/7 on-call and a named escalation path. Premium provides extended-hours coverage and an on-call P1 escalation during business hours + defined after-hours pager with slower response guarantees.
- Maintenance windows are scheduled and notified; credits apply only to unplanned downtime. We'll spell out exclusions.

I'm looping in Marissa to align on pricing and any possible reserved-capacity discounts for a 12/24 month commit. Diego, can you confirm whether we can include audit logs and a dedicated account success manager in the Platinum bundle for BrightHealth?

I'll attach our support tiers doc and a draft proposal by EOD 5/13.

Best,

Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_Support_Tiers_v2.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@brighthealth.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Premium support / uptime tiers for Dedicated (BrightHealth) -- pricing and options

Hi Sarah — following up with the pricing and concrete contract language. Summary (see attached Draft_MAAP_Proposal.pdf for full terms):

Tiers (monthly):
- Standard: 99.9% target availability; P1 ack 30m; P2 ack 4h; business-hours support; monthly price: $12,000.
- Premium: 99.95% target; P1 ack 15m; P2 ack 1h; extended-hours (06:00-24:00 local); monthly price: $20,000.
- Platinum: 99.99% target; P1 ack 15m + 24/7 on-call; P2 ack 30m; includes named escalation contacts + quarterly on-site (or virtual) runbook review; monthly price: $38,000.

Service credits (unplanned downtime over 30-day period):
- < 0.1% below target: 5% monthly credit
- 0.1%-0.5%: 15% credit
- > 0.5%: 50% credit (capped at 100% of monthly fee)
Credits are applied to the next invoice; retroactive cash refunds are not standard but negotiable for enterprise customers. Scheduled and notified maintenance windows are excluded from credit calculations; emergency maintenance will be evaluated case-by-case.

Discounts / packaging:
- 12-month reserved commit: 15% off list for Premium, 20% off for Platinum.
- 24-month commit: 20% off Premium, 25% off Platinum.
- For BrightHealth specifically, we can offer an additional one-time onboarding credit of up to 10% of the first 3 months' fees if you sign a 12-month Platinum commitment by May 25.

Add-ons included with Platinum (no additional monthly fee):
- Dedicated Customer Success Manager (CSM)
- Audit log retention (90 days) with export access
- Quarterly SLO reviews and proactive runbook tests

If you want audit logs pushed to your SIEM or longer retention, we can add that as an add-on. I've attached the draft MAAP for legal to review; it includes the formal credit table and definitions for P1/P2/P3.

Next steps: if this matches your expectations, I recommend a 30-min call Wed or Thu to walk procurement through the credit table and discount timing.

Regards,

Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Draft_MAAP_Proposal.pdf

From: Sarah Lin <sarah@brighthealth.com>

Subject: Re: Premium support / uptime tiers for Dedicated (BrightHealth) -- pricing and options

Marissa / Ava,

Thanks for the detail — this is helpful. A few clarifications before procurement can greenlight:
1) The credit cap: "capped at 100% of monthly fee"  does that mean the credit is limited to 100% for the month in which the downtime occurred? Any chance we can increase the cap for Platinum to 150% for an enterprise SLA breach?
2) Are emergency maintenance windows announced with at least X hours notice? We need specifics we can include in our contract.
3) For the onboarding credit tied to signing by May 25: is that a billing credit or reduced first invoice? Also, is the discount applied pro rata if we ramp capacity over the first quarter?

Were also interested in the audit log export option you mentioned — procurement will want export delivery details to confirm they meet our compliance needs.

Procurement notes were evaluating two vendors and will likely make a selection by May 20; the final questions above will help close. Can we do a short call Friday to confirm?

Thanks,

Sarah Lin
Head of Cloud Ops, BrightHealth

> Marissa / Ava,
>
> Thanks for the detail — this is helpful. A few clarifications before procurement can greenlight:
> 1) The credit cap: "capped at 100% of monthly fee" — does that mean the credit is limited to 100% for the month in which the downtime occurred? Any chance we can increase the cap for Platinum to 150% for an enterprise SLA breach?
> 2) Are emergency maintenance windows announced with at least X hours notice? We need specifics we can include in our contract.
> 3) For the onboarding credit tied to signing by May 25: is that a billing credit or reduced first invoice? Also, is the discount applied pro rata if we ramp capacity over the first quarter?

Hi Sarah — quick follow up from me. We can be flexible on a couple of items for BrightHealth given the scale and strategic nature of the deal:

- Credit cap: for Platinum we can increase the credit cap to 150% of the affected month's invoice for verified enterprise SLA breaches (requires joint post-incident review and acceptance of measurements).
- Emergency maintenance: we will strive to provide at least 4 hours notice for non-critical emergency maintenance; for critical hotfixes that require immediate action the contract will specify "as soon as practical" notification plus a post-event report.
- Onboarding credit: we'll apply it as a billing credit against the first two invoices (up to the value stated). If you ramp capacity during Q1, discounts are applied pro rata to the committed capacity baseline in the contract; variable overage pricing applies to incremental usage beyond the committed baseline.

If that sounds reasonable I can lock in the May 25 sign-by date for the onboarding credit and 20% Platinum discount with legal to get a more prescriptive clause into the draft MAAP. I added the HubSpot deal for tracking: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/48023.

Would you be available for a 20-minute call Monday (5/18) or Tuesday (5/19) to finalize?

Cheers,

Sean Gallagher
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (617) 555-0199
